articles.title: 7.7x Smaller and Encrypted at Rest: Compressing Symfony Messenger Payloads Without Touching a Handler
articles.excerpt: Symfony Messenger serializes a message, hands the bytes to a transport and forgets about them. Two things routinely go wrong with those bytes: They are too big. A bulk export, a sync job with a few th…
articles.body: Symfony Messenger serializes a message, hands the bytes to a transport and forgets about them. Two things routinely go wrong with those bytes: They are too big. A bulk export, a sync job with a few thousand rows, a report with embedded data, and you're past SQS's 256 KB limit or your Redis memory is going somewhere it shouldn't. They are readable. Names, emails, IBANs sit in plain text in messenger_messages , in a Redis RDB dump, on a RabbitMQ disk and in the dead-letter queue nobody has looked at since March. mattleads/messenger-compress-bundle fixes both at the transport-serializer layer. You opt in per message with a stamp or enforce a policy per transport, and your handlers receive the same plain PHP objects they always did.

articles.title: JPEG vs JPG: Is There Any Difference?
articles.excerpt: No. JPEG and JPG are the same image format. The only difference is the file extension: .jpeg has four letters and .jpg has three. Open the two files side by side and the picture data inside is built t…
articles.body: No. JPEG and JPG are the same image format. The only difference is the file extension: .jpeg has four letters and .jpg has three. Open the two files side by side and the picture data inside is built the same way. If that's all you wanted to know, you're done. If you'd like to understand why two spellings exist, and when the extension can still cause trouble, keep reading. Why are there two names? JPEG stands for Joint Photographic Experts Group, the committee that created the image standard in the early 1990s. The format is called JPEG. So where does "JPG" come from? Old Windows. Early versions of Windows, and the DOS file system under them, only allowed three letters after the dot in a filename. .jpeg didn't fit, so it was shortened to .jpg.

articles.title: Build Safer Link Previews for a Tencent RTC Community Chat
articles.excerpt: A casual community prompt—share a pet photo, story, or favorite animal link—creates a surprisingly serious backend decision: should your chat server automatically fetch every URL that members post? Au…
articles.body: A casual community prompt—share a pet photo, story, or favorite animal link—creates a surprisingly serious backend decision: should your chat server automatically fetch every URL that members post? Automatic previews make a social space easier to browse. They also turn your infrastructure into an HTTP client controlled by untrusted input. A malicious or accidental URL could target a loopback address, a private service, an oversized document, or a public URL that redirects somewhere private. The useful framing is not “Are link previews safe?” It is: Which URLs may the preview worker fetch, what state should members see, and what happens when the worker cannot safely decide? This tutorial builds that boundary in TypeScript.

articles.title: Handling Failures as Values in Agent-Generated Code
articles.excerpt: I am Jake Burwick, a high school student, and I built Vow, an open source programming language under the MIT license designed for AI agents to write. AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and C…
articles.body: I am Jake Burwick, a high school student, and I built Vow, an open source programming language under the MIT license designed for AI agents to write. AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor work in a continuous loop: write, run, read the error, fix. When agents write code in languages with null values and implicit exceptions, failure paths are easily overlooked. An unhandled exception or a missing null check causes a runtime crash later in execution. Vow has no nulls and no exceptions. Result Values in Vow In Vow, functions that can fail return Result values. Every failure is represented directly as a value. Functions return Result values that must be handled with match or the ? operator. Here is how failure is handled in Vow: fn parsePrice(text) { let n = num(text)?

This post fixes the first one, hands-on and from scratch: delete-then-INSERT leaves a window where Athena readers see an empty partition, and if the INSERT fails, the partition stays empty until the next run. Thanks, Karan. Here is the full pattern, with a demo you can run in your own account and tear down afterwards. 1. The problem: the empty window With delete-then-insert, the partition goes through three states: Between the delete and the end of the insert , every query on that partition returns zero rows. A dashboard refreshing at that moment shows a hole. If the insert fails , nothing restores the old data.

articles.body: How we score an election forecast (and what the score does not measure) TL;DR: We score the reasoning before the outcome. Each answer is rated 0 to 100 on specificity, grounding and calibration by a fixed judge. After certification we add winner accuracy, calibration curves and the Brier score. A model can be wrong and score well; a vague answer always scores badly. The protocol is public at elections.lforla.org/methodology.html . 1. Pre-registration Every answer was collected before the vote, between 26 August and 31 October 2026, and is published verbatim. The date attached to each model is the date its forecast entered the benchmark. This matters more than any scoring detail. If a forecast can be edited after the first results, the score measures hindsight, not forecasting.

articles.title: James Webb Space Telescope uncovers new clues about the origins of 'interstellar invader' comet 3I/ATLAS
articles.excerpt: The findings are another clue towards understanding the origins of 3I/ATLAS and the planet-forming conditions around other stars.
articles.body: Using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), scientists have found that the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS was built from tiny grains of ice mixed with dust that are quite different from the solar system’s comets. These ice grains do, however, bear striking similarities to some icy bodies located at the edge of the solar system, beyond the orbit of Neptune, so-called trans-Neptunian objects (TNOs). 3I/ATLAS was discovered entering the solar system in the summer of 2025. It was only the third object found entering the solar system from farther afield in the Milky Way after 1I/'Oumuamua , seen in 2017, and 2I/Borisov , detected in 2019. This meant the interstellar comet offered a rare chance to glimpse the conditions under which such bodies form in other star systems.

articles.body: On Nov. 2, 2000, the International Space Station welcomed its first long-term residents: NASA astronaut Bill Shepherd and two Russian cosmonauts, Yuri Gidzenko and Sergei Krikalev. The mission was called Expedition 1. Before this expedition, NASA had launched five, one-week-long Space Shuttle missions to help build the space station and bring up supplies. But this time, the crew would be staying for four and a half months, and they weren't taking the shuttle. Instead, they took a Russian Soyuz spacecraft , and this was the first Soyuz to ever dock at the space station. During their stay at the space station, they unpacked supplies and installed new equipment, including the first solar arrays.
